content:
rafa: Quick thread: proposal to support ephemeral project-scoped delegation from org API keys. Trying to balance operator convenience vs auditable least-privilege.
jin: Can you explain the use-case? Sounds like minting short-lived project tokens from a long-lived org key?
rafa: Exactly. Many infra jobs use an org key in CI to create project resources. We could let the service mint an ephemeral project token with limited TTL & scope, recorded in audit.
maria: Slightly worried about adding more token minting surface; historically those flows cause too-broad privileges by default.
viktor: Implementation sketch: add an endpoint POST /keys/:id/delegate that requires admin scope on the org key and returns a delegated token with claims {project, allowed_actions, expires_at}. The org key must have delegate=true flag.
jin: Sounds OK if delegate=true is admin-only and the endpoint enforces a max TTL (e.g., 1h) and whitelist of allowed actions.
auth-bot: [policy] token_class change: key=k_org_42 actor=ops admin_approval=true flag=delegate:true recorded_at=1723459070
rafa: Audit + transparency requirements: each delegation must emit an audit record with parent_key, child_token_id, intended_project, allowed_actions, actor, justification. Also provide an API to list active delegated tokens.
maria: Also require opt-in mapping: when delegating into a project, the resulting token should map to a constrained role (e.g., project-delegate) not inherit full org roles. Prevent privilege inflation.
viktor: Agree. Role resolution for delegated tokens = intersection(orig_key_roles, requested_action_set, project_policy). If intersection empty -> reject.
jin: Edge-case: what about rate-limits? If org key used to mint lots of delegated tokens, we could DoS project quotas. Need throttling per parent key and per org.
auth-bot: [metric] key=k_org_42 delegation_attempts=7 window=60s throttle_threshold=10
rafa: Good catch. Add per-key delegation QPS and a global delegation budget per org. Reject with 429 and an auth error when exceeded.
maria: Cache/invalidations: delegated tokens are short-lived so don't require expensive invalidation; but revocation must be supported: add revoke endpoint that marks token revoked and publishes revoke event. Gateways check revocation list (cache with TTL).
viktor: For offline gateways, revocation eventual consistency is OK for short TTLs; but for high-sensitivity actions we should require synchronous checks against auth service (configurable).
jin: UX asks: console should show "Active delegations" per key + quick revoke and export CSV for audits.
auth-bot: [event] delegation-created id=dt_77 parent=k_org_42 project=proj-13 actor=ci-bot ttl_s=3600
rafa: Migration notes: don't create delegate=true for existing org keys by default. Provide a migration CLI to propose delegation-safe splits and to add delegate flag per-key with audit justification.
maria: Summary for RFC follow-up: 1) new delegate endpoint with admin-only delegate flag, 2) delegated tokens limited TTL + allowed_actions whitelist, 3) role intersection mapping, 4) per-key/org throttles, 5) audit records + list/revoke APIs, 6) console views + migration tooling, 7) revoke propagation policy documented.
jin: LGTM. Add a note: revoke must set a short negative-cache TTL to speed up enforcement for critical revocations.
viktor: Also add tests: fuzz delegation requests, ensure intersection denies privilege escalation, and load test throttles.
rafa: I'll draft the RFC follow-up and include example request/response snippets. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
